aspects.says: A -c command runs in a second JVM on deploy-cli/ and sees only its own registry; the running node is read over its SSH CLI.
basis: section:17.5 A Command Sees Only the JVM It Runs In

aspects.says: SystemMonitor's drift shows a pause only where it covers the monitor's wake-up; the GC log records every pause.
basis: section:17.6 `drift` Shows a Pause Only When It Covers the Monitor's Wake-Up

aspects.says: How a DirPoll processor ends decides where the file goes: returned bytes to response/ and the file to archive/, a retry exception back to request/ after ten poll intervals, any other exception to bad/.
basis: section:17.2 How the Processor Ends Decides Where the File Goes

aspects.says: Processing must be idempotent, keyed by the batch's identity in its content and recorded with the postings, never by the file name.
basis: section:17.4 A Stop or a Crash Leaves Files in `run/`, Some of Them Already Done

aspects.says: One processor instance handles every file, so nothing about one file is kept in fields.
basis: section:17.1 A Batch Directory Under Q2

aspects.says: A retry waits on a pool thread and DirPoll counts no attempts, so a file that can never improve stalls every file behind it and should be refused instead.
basis: section:17.2 How the Processor Ends Decides Where the File Goes

aspects.says: A stop or a crash leaves files in run/, some done and some never started, and nothing moves them back.
basis: section:17.4 A Stop or a Crash Leaves Files in `run/`, Some of Them Already Done

aspects.says: DirPoll takes a file the moment it appears, so a processor treats a missing trailer or an empty file as not finished, and the sender writes elsewhere and renames.
basis: section:17.3 DirPoll Takes a File the Moment It Appears, Finished or Not
